example_directive: Make the migration idempotent: re-running inserts nothing new, updates converge, and the test is literally "run twice, diff zero."

implied_procedure: Group the state changes so no intermediate state is observable: all apply or none; define the single commit point where the change becomes real; everything before it is revertible for free, everything after is not.
replaces_instruction: Make it all-or-nothing: no reader can ever see the half-done state — and know exactly which instruction is the point of no return.
ambiguities: Physics sense (indivisible) borrowed; in distributed systems, atomic commit is a protocol (2PC) with its own liveness costs; "atomic" in casual planning use means "as one unit" — say which.
example_directive: The rename + repoint must be atomic: both or neither, readers see old or new; the config swap is the commit point — everything before it rolls back clean.

implied_procedure: Where atomic commit is impossible (cross-system, no shared transaction), define for each step an explicit semantic undo; execute steps in order; on failure run compensations in reverse; the end state is consistent, though not identical to never-started.
replaces_instruction: Since these two systems can't share a transaction, write the undo for every step before you take it — and when step 4 fails, run the undos backward from there.
ambiguities: Compensation restores consistency, not history (an email sent stays sent); silently weaker than rollback — the residual trace must be documented per step.
example_directive: No 2PC across the CRM and billing APIs: write compensating actions for each call in the saga, execute in order, compensate in reverse on failure, and log the residual state.

implied_procedure: Read state with its version; compute the change; apply only if the version is unchanged since the read; on conflict, discard and retry from fresh state — never merge blind.
replaces_instruction: Check the world still looks like it did when you decided: apply the write only if nothing moved underneath you, and if it did, start over from the new reality.
ambiguities: Contrast with pessimistic locking (lock first, wait); retry loops under contention need backoff (§ below); the pattern's name in instruction form is "revalidate at use."
example_directive: CAS the config update: apply only if resourceVersion still matches what you read; on mismatch, re-read, rediff, and try once more before reporting conflict.

implied_procedure: Immediately before destructive change, capture restorable state (dump, tag, image); verify the snapshot restorable-ness; only then mutate; the snapshot outlives the change's verification window.
replaces_instruction: Take the backup you'd curse yourself for skipping — and prove it can be restored — before you touch anything you can't rebuild.
ambiguities: A snapshot without a restore test is a comfort blanket; also distinct from WAL (which records intent, not just state).
example_directive: Snapshot the accounts table (pg_dump, tag the file, restore-probe into a scratch DB) before the column type change — the probe is part of the snapshot.

implied_procedure: Record intended actions durably before executing them; execution follows the log; on crash, replay the log from the checkpoint; the log is the truth of intent.
replaces_instruction: Write down what you're about to do where it survives crashes, then do it — so any interruption resumes from the record instead of from guesswork.
ambiguities: Database heritage; applied to agents it means an externalized durable intent record (§18 state externalization is the general form); replay must be idempotent or the guarantee collapses.
example_directive: WAL the migration: append each intended DDL statement to the journal before executing; the recovery procedure replays the journal idempotently and reports position.

implied_procedure: Execute the full path with effects suppressed or diverted to a disposable sink; capture everything the real run would do; diff intended-vs-actual; a clean dry run is the ticket's evidence, not its substitute.
replaces_instruction: Walk the whole thing through without touching anything real — show me exactly what it would do, then we compare that against what we meant.
ambiguities: Coverage varies: some dry runs skip validation, some suppress only writes; "measure twice, cut once" is the folk ancestor; a dry run in a stale environment certifies nothing.
example_directive: Dry-run the bulk edit: full parse and full diff against a copy; the diff is the review artifact — zero surprises at execution time is the bar.

implied_procedure: Enumerate every mutation the work could perform; confine them to declared boundaries (paths, tables, endpoints); verify the boundary holds (read-only mounts, blocked egress); undeclared side effects are defects.
replaces_instruction: Decide up front the only places this work is allowed to change anything — and enforce that fence mechanically, so exploration can't damage what it wasn't sent to touch.
ambiguities: Boundary enforcement must be mechanical (mounts, policies), not behavioral (good intentions); research tasks need it most exactly when they feel least dangerous.
example_directive: Analysis is read-only: mount the repo RO, writes go to /tmp/out only, network limited to the registry; any other observed write is a bug report.

implied_procedure: Build once, name the artifact by its content hash; never modify in place; "change" means build a new artifact and repoint; rollback is repointing to a prior name.
replaces_instruction: Whatever we deploy is a frozen, content-addressed thing — you don't edit it, you build its successor and switch the pointer; reverting is just pointing back.
ambiguities: Immutable artifacts vs. immutable infrastructure (whole environments from templates); requires content addressing or signatures to mean anything under adversarial conditions.
example_directive: Ship the container as an immutable artifact tagged by digest; the deploy references the digest, and "hotfix in prod" is disabled by policy and by registry.

implied_procedure: Fix every dependency to an exact version (digest where possible); record them in a lockfile that is itself versioned; upgrades happen as reviewed, isolated changes with their own tests; floating ranges are prohibited in CI.
replaces_instruction: Nail every dependency down exactly, keep the nails in the repo, and make upgrading a deliberate reviewed act — not something the build does to us overnight.
ambiguities: Lockfile honesty (transitives included?) varies by ecosystem; pinning without an upgrade cadence trades rot for stagnation — schedule it.
example_directive: Pin the toolchain in the lockfile including transitive digests; `latest` anywhere in CI is a failed check; upgrades ride their own PR with the diff suite.

implied_procedure: Make outputs depend only on declared inputs: fixed toolchain, vendored deps, no network at build time, no ambient state (clock, locale, env); identical inputs produce bit-identical outputs.
replaces_instruction: The build can only use what it declares and carries — nothing from the network, nothing from the build machine's mood — so the same commit always produces the same artifact, anywhere, forever.
ambiguities: Hermetic (sealed inputs) vs. reproducible (same output) — related, not identical; timestamp/locale/locale-embedded paths are the classic leaks.
example_directive: Make the release build hermetic: vendored deps, fixed toolchain digests, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH set, network disabled in the builder — then bit-compare two builds on different hosts.

implied_procedure: Record the full input stream; on demand, re-execute from a checkpoint against the recorded stream; the execution follows the identical path; divergence is itself a monitored signal.
replaces_instruction: Keep everything needed to make it happen again exactly as it happened — same inputs, same order, same result — so failures can be studied at full fidelity offline.
ambiguities: Requires disciplined capture (including time, randomness seeds, external responses); replay fidelity is only as good as the capture's completeness — unrecorded side channels break it silently.
example_directive: Enable deterministic replay on the order service: record ingress and external responses; any Sev-1 gets replayed in staging with assertions on the divergence points.

implied_procedure: Apply the change retroactively to historical records: define the transformation, the batch boundaries, and the idempotency key; run incrementally with checkpoints; verify counts and samples old-vs-new; the backfill is re-runnable after interruption.
replaces_instruction: Fix the old data too, not just the code: run the transformation over history in resumable batches, prove the row counts and spot-checks agree, and make sure an interrupted run can just be started again.
ambiguities: Forward-fix vs. backfill semantics must be stated (does the new code handle old rows, or does the migration rewrite them?); silent dual-code-paths during the window are the trap.
example_directive: Backfill the currency field in 10k-row batches keyed by id: checkpointed, idempotent, count-reconciled — and the old reader path stays until the backfill reports 100% twice.

implied_procedure: Detect the deviation from correct state; restore correctness; then verify the restoration by measurement against the correct-state definition; the word claims the error is gone, not merely addressed.
replaces_instruction: Put it back to right — and then check it's actually right against the definition of right, because "I did a fix" and "it is correct now" are different claims.
ambiguities: Weaker uses mean "adjusted"; the repair-verify pairing is the procedural core; silently conflated with remediate (fixing the class, § below).
example_directive: Rectify the drifted shard: re-sync from primary, then diff row counts and checksums — the verification is the completion criterion, not the sync command's exit code.

implied_procedure: Beyond fixing the instance: identify the class of defect, remove the class (control, generator, pattern), and verify by searching for siblings of the same class; the same defect cannot recur through that path.
replaces_instruction: Don't just patch this one — find every other place this same mistake lives, fix the mechanism that produced them, and sweep to prove no siblings remain.
ambiguities: Security-remediation sense (close the vuln class) vs. HR sense (rehabilitate a person); distinct from rectify (instance) — remediation targets the class; "rehabilitate" as a sibling term is best reserved for restoring a compromised account/system to trust.
example_directive: The off-by-one is fixed — now remediate: grep for the pattern that generated it, fix all five call sites, and add the lint rule that makes the class unrepresentable.

implied_procedure: Map every equivalent representation to the single canonical form before comparison, storage, or deduplication; the normalization rules are explicit and versioned; transformations are idempotent.
replaces_instruction: Make everything that means the same thing look the same way first — one canonical encoding, applied identically everywhere — or your comparisons lie to you.
ambiguities: Canonicalization sense vs. statistical normalization (scaling) vs. the failure to normalize deviance (§12 — opposite valence entirely); "canonical" (§17) names the chosen form.
example_directive: Normalize keys to NFC snake_case before the merge; the rule table is versioned in the repo, and the dedup count is reported before we drop rows.

implied_procedure: On retryable failure, wait an exponentially growing interval with a random component (jitter) added; cap the total attempts and the total time; non-retryable failures bypass the loop entirely.
replaces_instruction: When it fails, wait a bit longer each time plus some randomness — so a thousand synchronized clients don't hammer in lockstep — and give up after a stated number of tries.
ambiguities: The jitter is the part everyone drops, and it's the part that prevents thundering herds; exponential-without-jitter is synchronized self-harm; retry budgets vs. attempt caps differ.
example_directive: Retry the upstream with backoff and jitter: base 200ms, ×2, ±30% jitter, 5 attempts max, then circuit-break and report.

implied_procedure: Whatever was validated at check time is revalidated at use time: the world is allowed to change between your check and your action, so bind the check's result to the action's input.
replaces_instruction: Look again right before you leap — between when you checked the condition and when you act on it, the condition may have died; check-and-act must be one atomic motion.
ambiguities: Security-heritage acronym (time-of-check to time-of-use) opaque to newcomers — the parenthetical expansion is the usable form; race-condition framing makes the fix (locking or CAS) clearer.
example_directive: TOCTOU guard the cleanup: re-stat and re-verify the path is still the scanned file inside the unlink, or hold the fd you validated.

implied_procedure: Draw the explicit boundary of the work: what is in, what is out, and the interface between them; the out-list is written, not implied; boundary disputes are resolved by consulting the delineation, not by renegotiating silently.
replaces_instruction: Write down exactly where this task's responsibility starts and stops — with an explicit not-this list — so expansions have a document to violate instead of a vibe to argue with.
ambiguities: Medium density: the artifact (the written boundary) is the value; without the out-list it's a synonym for "describe."
example_directive: Delineate the integration task: in-scope = auth and sync; out-of-scope = billing UI, reporting, schema redesign; anything else found gets a decision, not a shrug and absorption.

implied_procedure: Rank the items by a declared key (value × urgency × dependency-blocking); break ties by the key, not by requester volume; the ranking is visible and re-derived when inputs change.
replaces_instruction: Put these in a defensible order and tell me the rule you used — because "everything's important" is a scheduling deadlock, and loudest-voice is the default key we're replacing.
ambiguities: Without the declared key it's a power move, not a procedure; priority-inversion (low-key items blocking high-key ones through dependencies) is the classic failure of naive ranking.
example_directive: Prioritize the backlog by blocked-downstream × revenue-at-risk; publish the sort key with the list, and flag any item whose rank is a judgment call.

implied_procedure: Write the finished outcome first (the press release, the user story in the past tense); derive from it the minimum set of deliverables; each deliverable justifies itself by trace to the outcome or gets cut.
replaces_instruction: Describe the end state as if it already exists, then work out what must be true for that sentence to be honest — everything that doesn't make the sentence true is out of scope.
ambiguities: Distinct from inversion (§2: reason from failure) — this is derivation from the finished state; product-heritage (press-release method); without the trace-to-outcome step it decays to vision-statement theater.
example_directive: Write the launch press release first; every workstream must cite the sentence it makes true, or it's cut.

implied_procedure: Define completion as observable conditions checked against reality (not activities performed); the criteria are fixed before execution starts; work ends when they hold, regardless of remaining enthusiasm.
replaces_instruction: Define "done" as measurable states of the world — then stop when the world is in that state; we don't stop when the tasks run out, and we don't continue because the tasks were fun.
ambiguities: Exit criteria (we may stop) vs. acceptance criteria (the deliverable qualifies) vs. abort criteria (§4: we must stop); tasks-completed is the counterfeit version of all three.
example_directive: Exit criteria for the incident: error budget restored, cause identified with evidence, one preventive action merged. Not "postmortem written" — that's an activity, not a state.

implied_procedure: Attach to each unit of work a fixed completion checklist (tests, docs, review, telemetry, rollback path); the unit is not done until every item holds; the list is identical across units, changed only by process decision.
replaces_instruction: Done means the same thing every time: tested, reviewed, documented, observable, reversible — not "the code is written," which is where amateurs put the finish line.
ambiguities: DoD (per-unit quality bar) vs. exit criteria (per-effort end state) vs. acceptance criteria (per-deliverable contract); a DoD nobody verifies on merge is a poster.
example_directive: Definition of done here: tests green, README updated, metric emitted, rollback documented — the PR template enforces all four checkboxes, and "partial done" doesn't parse.

implied_procedure: Generate genuinely distinct candidate plans (not variants of the first); state each one's assumptions, cost, and failure signature; wargame each against the criteria; select the survivor with the rejected options recorded.
replaces_instruction: Build at least three actually-different ways to do this, pressure-test each against our constraints and failure scenarios, choose one, and keep the losers on file with the reason they lost.
ambiguities: Military planning heritage; the common decay is three costumes on one plan; the recorded-rejection step is what keeps it honest when circumstances change.
example_directive: Three COAs for the capacity crunch (split service, cache aggressively, buy hardware): assumptions, cost, failure mode each; wargame against Black-Friday load; document the selection.

implied_procedure: Identify the foreseen decision points; preplan the alternative taken at each (branch) and the follow-on after success (sequel); the plan carries its own decision tree; at the point, you choose, you don't design.
replaces_instruction: Decide now what we'll do if the cheap path fails at each known fork, and what we'll do next if it succeeds — so the future decision is a selection among prepared moves, not an all-hands panic.
ambiguities: Military doctrinal terms; adjacent to implementation intentions (if-then precommitments) in psychology; branches without named decision points drift into generic contingency lists.
example_directive: Branches for the rollout: 5xx at canary → hold, shard by cohort, or abort — each fully specified. Sequel on clean 24h: full fleet by Friday.

implied_procedure: Build the dependency graph with durations; compute the longest chain to completion; that chain's slack is zero — protect it, staff it, and re-derive it when any node moves; delays off-path are recoverable, delays on-path are not.
replaces_instruction: Find the chain of tasks where every day lost is a day lost forever — that's where attention and people go first; everything else has slack and can wait.
ambiguities: Critical-chain variant folds resource contention into the path; the method's honesty depends on duration estimates, which are chronically optimistic (§12 outside view applies).
example_directive: Recompute the critical path weekly; anything that lands on it gets its own risk line in the status; off-path slippage gets one sentence.

implied_procedure: Name the one decisive task that receives priority of scarce resources; every other task gets the minimum that keeps it viable; resource conflicts resolve toward the main effort by standing rule.
replaces_instruction: Pick the thing that decides this week and concentrate everything on it — everything else runs on fumes by design, and that's not neglect, it's arithmetic.
ambiguities: Military doctrine heritage; misread as "prioritize" (ranking) — this is allocation plus a conflict-resolution rule; without a named single main effort, everything is the main effort and nothing is.
example_directive: Main effort this month is checkout latency: conflicts resolve toward it; reporting and feature polish get minimum-viable hours, recorded as deliberate, not accidental.

implied_procedure: Fix the duration and let scope flex: when the box ends, work stops and the deliverable is whatever honestly exists; the box's end is a hard stop, pre-agreed, with results reported either way.
replaces_instruction: You have exactly this long — when it's up, you stop and show what you have; scope is the variable, the clock isn't, and "almost" counts as done-with-gaps to report.
ambiguities: Not a deadline (scope fixed, date flexes) — the inversion matters; timeboxing exploration prevents rabbit holes, but timeboxing surgery would be insane — match the tool to the reversibility of the work.
example_directive: Timebox the parser investigation to 4 hours: at the bell, report findings, confidence, and recommended next box — not a half-finished rewrite.

implied_procedure: Run a bounded experiment whose deliverable is knowledge, not production code: state the question, the time budget, and the decision the answer feeds; the artifact is discarded or rebuilt to standard afterward.
replaces_instruction: Go find out cheaply whether this approach can work — fixed hours, one question to answer, and whatever code you write to learn it gets thrown away or rewritten properly.
ambiguities: The discard clause is the most-violated term (spikes graduate into production by inertia); traffic-spike polysemy applies; a spike without a decision it feeds is tourism.
example_directive: Two-day spike: can the JIT handle our IR? Answer by Friday with a recommendation and a number; the prototype code is already scheduled for deletion.

implied_procedure: Before optimizing any single stage, drive one thin real instance end-to-end through every stage with production-shape interfaces; fix only what blocks passage; then widen each stage in place.
replaces_instruction: Get one real request all the way through the whole pipeline first — ugly but genuine, every stage touched — because integrating skeletons early is cheap and integrating Big Bangs never happens.
ambiguities: Analog, not literal ordnance; distinct from prototype (which explores feasibility) — this builds the real structure thinly; the discipline is resisting stage-local perfection.
example_directive: Tracer first: one genuine order from webhook to ledger through the real services and schemas; only then does any stage get tuned.

implied_procedure: Schedule the decision point with named criteria and a named decider; evidence is presented against each criterion; a single unmet criterion is a no-go unless the decider explicitly waives it with a recorded reason.
replaces_instruction: At this checkpoint we stop and decide with a checklist: every criterion shown, someone accountable says go or no-go, and any waiver is written down with who and why.
ambiguities: Gate criteria without owners decay into group nodding; distinct from abort criteria (mid-flight stops); "go with conditions" should mean conditions with owners and dates or it means nothing.
example_directive: Go/no-go Friday 15:00: replication lag < 2s, backup restored in staging, on-call briefed, rollback rehearsed. Any red stops us; waivers need the EM's name on them.

implied_procedure: Hold work to the delineated objective: discovered adjacent work is logged, triaged, and scheduled — not absorbed; the standing question is "does this serve the stated objective," and the default answer to expansion is a new ticket.
replaces_instruction: When you find more work than you were given, write it down and hand it back — don't do it silently; the task either finishes as defined or the definition changes through an explicit decision.
ambiguities: Over-tight containment blocks legitimately discovered prerequisites — the repair is escalation and re-scoping, not silent refusal; distinguish scope creep (expansion) from gold-plating (unrequested polish).
example_directive: Scope stays the stated objective: anything discovered that doesn't serve it gets a ticket and one summary line — the fifth such line triggers a scope conversation with the owner.

implied_procedure: Classify each decision by reversibility: two-way (cheap to undo) → decide fast with partial information; one-way (expensive or impossible to undo) → deliberate, verify, and get independent review; when in doubt, run the cheap experiment that converts one-way to two-way.
replaces_instruction: Is this reversible? If undoing it costs an afternoon, decide now and move; if undoing it is impossible or ruinous, slow down, check twice, and get a second set of eyes before pulling it.
ambiguities: Classification is itself sometimes wrong (the disguised one-way door is the classic catastrophe); irreversibility can be graded, and the test is the cost of the return path, not the drama of the choice.
example_directive: Schema drops, key rotations, and public disclosures are one-way doors — full review before any of them. Everything else in this task is a two-way door: decide within the hour.

implied_procedure: Justify every element from current goals and current facts; inherited defaults carry zero weight; the burden falls on each existing component to re-earn its place; deletion is the default verdict for what cannot justify itself.
replaces_instruction: Assume nothing deserves to exist just because it already does: rebuild the justification for every piece from what we're trying to do now, and whatever can't argue for itself goes.
ambiguities: Finance origin (zero-based budgeting); expensive at full scope — apply to the load-bearing layer, not the office supplies; hostile to accumulated tacit knowledge if applied with a chainsaw instead of a scalpel.
example_directive: Zero-base the alert rules: each one re-justifies against current SLOs or dies; "it's always been there" is not a justification, and the quarterly alert-fatigue number proves why.

implied_procedure: These adjectives assert completeness without a closure rule; the repair is mechanical: define the generating rule for the set, the count, and the verification that the count is satisfied; then the adjective is either earned or retracted.
replaces_instruction: Comprehensive, "holistic," and bare "end-to-end" mean nothing checkable — replace each with: which set, defined how, totaling what, verified against what count.
ambiguities: The words feel like rigor and function as scope inflation; "end-to-end" survives with a stated path ("from webhook to ledger, every hop named"); the other two should generally be retired from directives.
example_directive: Strike "comprehensive" from the audit plan; replace with: the 214 endpoints from the registry list, reconciled against the route table count, delta explained.

implied_procedure: Implement the minimum change that tests the hypothesis or closes the need; speculative generality is deferred until a present requirement demands it; every addition carries a cost line (build, test, maintain, explain).
replaces_instruction: Do the least that solves the actual problem — no framework for future problems we don't have, no abstraction for one caller — additions wait for a second concrete need.
ambiguities: Misread as sloppiness: YAGNI governs feature scope, not quality of what's built (tests and clarity are not "speculative"); the standing counterweight is that some cheap-now provisions (logging) are brutal to retrofit.
example_directive: Smallest viable change: add the cache header, not the CDN; measure; if the p75 stays bad, the CDN becomes a real proposal instead of a preemptive one.

implied_procedure: Scale the response's intensity to the harm prevented and the values at stake: name the metric the response is proportional to; verify no materially weaker response achieves the same end; excess is itself a defect.
replaces_instruction: Match force to stakes: before the strong measure, show the weaker one was tried or ruled out on stated grounds — because overshooting is a failure mode, not a safety margin.
ambiguities: Proportionate to what? (risk, cost, harm, authority granted — must be named); law-of-armed-conflict sense is the strict ancestor; unanchored, the word launders whatever response was preferred anyway.
example_directive: Proportionality check on the IP block: one abusive tenant → one tenant block, 15-minute TTL; the /24 is disproportionate unless the per-tenant block demonstrably failed.

implied_procedure: Change exactly the target and nothing else: minimal incision, maximal preservation of surrounding tissue (code, state, behavior); collateral edits are prohibited by default and each requires its own justification.
replaces_instruction: Touch only the thing that's broken — no drive-by refactors, no reformatting, no "while I'm here"; the diff shows the defect and nothing but the defect.
ambiguities: Medical metaphor implies both precision and restraint — either alone is a scalpel waved in the wrong direction; clashes with improvement culture ("while we're in there"), which must be explicitly overruled.
example_directive: Surgical fix only: the one predicate clause and its test. Format-only diffs, renamed variables, and adjacent cleanups all get reverted on sight.

implied_procedure: The restraint triad: judicious = weigh alternatives before acting and say what you weighed; parsimonious = spend the minimum resource that meets the need (Occam applied to action); discriminating = draw fine distinctions between cases that deserve different treatment.
replaces_instruction: Think before spending, spend the least that works, and treat different cases differently — the three together forbid both recklessness and blanket uniform responses.
ambiguities: As bare adjectives each is praise, not procedure — they steer only when the decision-trace (what was weighed, what was spent, which distinctions were drawn) is demanded as the artifact.
example_directive: Be judicious, parsimonious, and discriminating here — concretely: log the alternative you rejected, the resource floor you chose, and the case feature that justified different treatment.

implied_procedure: The enforcement pentad, each a different act: mandate = make X required (absence of X is a violation); prohibit = make X forbidden (presence of X is a violation); enforce = detect violations mechanically and apply consequences reliably; uphold = personally refuse to violate despite pressure; preserve = actively maintain an invariant against decay.
replaces_instruction: Say which kind of rule this is: required, forbidden, mechanically-checked-with-consequences, personally-guarded-under-pressure, or maintained-against-drift — each implies different infrastructure and different failure modes.
ambiguities: Casual use swaps them freely ("we mandate security" meaning none of the five); enforcement without detection is aspiration; preserve is the weakest-sounding and most operational (an invariant needing active maintenance decays the moment maintenance stops).
example_directive: We prohibit plaintext secrets (presence = violation, scanner enforces), mandate review on the merge path (CI enforces), and you uphold both under deadline pressure — preserve means the checks themselves get maintenance tickets, not quiet rot.

implied_procedure: Partition all available actions by reversibility and blast radius: irreversible or wide-blast actions require explicit approval first; reversible, contained actions proceed immediately with a report after; the partition is written down in advance.
replaces_instruction: Decide now which actions need permission and which need forgiveness: destructive, external, or one-way moves wait for a yes; everything else goes now and shows up in the log.
ambiguities: The partition is the policy — without it written, each action re-litigates the category mid-flight (slow) or guesses it (dangerous); "ask" has a latency cost that itself can be the failure mode in time-critical work.
example_directive: Ask-before-act: deletions, external sends, spending, anything one-way. Act-then-report: everything else, logged. When unsure which list an action is on, it's on the first.

implied_procedure: Pre-grant specific authority within written bounds (what, where, when, how much); exercise within bounds requires no further approval; every exercise is logged; exceeding bounds is not a gray zone, it's unauthorized.
replaces_instruction: Here's what you may do without asking each time — the exact actions, the exact limits — and everything past those limits still needs a human, every time.
ambiguities: Grants erode into assumed broader permissions ("it worked last time" ≠ authority); review cadence is part of the grant, not an afterthought; the log is what makes the grant auditable rather than anecdotal.
example_directive: Standing authorization: restart any non-prod service, up to 3×/day, logged. Prod restarts, schema changes, and third restarts of the same service: ask.

implied_procedure: Test each contemplated action against the grant of authority that empowers this work: if the action exceeds the grant's scope, it is void regardless of its merits; the correct move is to surface the need and request the authority.
replaces_instruction: Check the action is actually inside what you were empowered to do — outside that line, even a good idea is not yours to execute; report the gap instead of filling it yourself.
ambiguities: Corporate-law origin; the doctrine's force depends on the authority document being written (a charter, a task brief, an envelope); "clearly they'd want this" is the standard rationalization it exists to block.
example_directive: Editing the billing plan is ultra vires for this engagement: note the need in the report, request the authority, touch nothing in that subsystem.

implied_procedure: Act strictly in the principal's interest: conflicts of interest are disclosed before acting; self-dealing is structurally excluded; discretion is exercised as the principal would exercise it with the same information, and the loyalty runs to them, not to your convenience.
replaces_instruction: You are trusted with someone else's interests: when your interests and theirs diverge, say so out loud first, and make every call the one they'd make if they stood where you stand.
ambiguities: Legal standard from trust law, applied by analogy — its content is the conflict-disclosure discipline, not the vibe of responsibility; agent self-preservation (hiding mistakes) is the commonest quiet breach.
example_directive: Fiduciary posture on this account: any action that advantages your own convenience over their latency budget gets disclosed before it's taken, and errors surface the moment they're suspected.

term: Primum non nocere (first, do no harm)
implied_procedure: Under uncertainty about an intervention's safety, order the options by harm potential; the no-action or least-invasive option is the default; the burden falls on intervention to prove itself safer than waiting.
replaces_instruction: When you're not sure whether the fix helps or hurts, the safe default is to not touch it — inaction is a choice you're allowed, and "we had to do something" is the excuse it exists to refuse.
ambiguities: Inaction also has harms (the omission trap) — the doctrine biases correctly only when intervention's harm distribution is the wider one; in incident response under a degrading system, it can rationalize fatal passivity: state which failure mode you're guarding against.
example_directive: On the healthy replica: first, do no harm — no restart, no config touch; the invasive options wait for the failed node's autopsy.

implied_procedure: When evidence is split between options, choose the one whose error you can survive: prefer the reversible, the contained, the well-understood, and the maintainable; novelty carries a surcharge that must be paid down with evidence.
replaces_instruction: When you genuinely can't tell, take the choice whose worst case we've already survived — the boring, undoable, local one — and let the exotic option win only on evidence, not on enthusiasm.
ambiguities: Bias is usually an error, and here it's a policy — scope-limited to genuine uncertainty; overapplied it becomes permanent stagnation (the established option gets an unearned home-team advantage forever).
example_directive: Two candidate fixes, evidence split: ship the reversible local patch tonight; the architectural rewrite needs its own evidence, not our fatigue.

implied_procedure: Defer intervention deliberately, not negligently: define the metrics watched, their thresholds, the check cadence, and the criterion that converts waiting into acting; the waiting itself is a prescribed state with an owner.
replaces_instruction: We're not ignoring this, we're monitoring it on purpose: here's what we watch, here's the number that changes our minds, and until then, hands off.
ambiguities: Distinct from procrastination by the existence of the conversion trigger; without thresholds and cadence it's the omission trap wearing a clinical name.
example_directive: Watchful waiting on the index bloat: weekly measurement, act if scan latency doubles or the Friday number degrades two weeks running; otherwise, no action before Q3.

implied_procedure: Deliberately reduce the intensity or tempo of an interaction or process: step down force levels one rung at a time, signal the reduction explicitly, maintain the escape path for the other party, and never de-escalate past your own safety floor.
replaces_instruction: Turn the temperature down on purpose: reduce the provocation level, say you're doing it, leave them a face-saving exit — but keep your own protective floor intact the whole way down.
ambiguities: Conflict sense vs. clinical therapy sense vs. infrastructure sense (de-escalating privileges, load); in ops contexts, de-escalating load (shedding, throttling) is the systems translation; misread as capitulation by cultures that equate firmness with volume.
example_directive: De-escalate the incident bridge: single spokesperson, status every 15 minutes, no blame language; in parallel, de-escalate the system — shed load, throttle ingest, hold feature flags.

implied_procedure: A universal, unconditional halt signal during live operations: on receipt, stop all actions immediately, preserve current state, hold position, and await further instruction; it overrides every other priority including completion.
replaces_instruction: These words end everything mid-stream: freeze, keep the state exactly as it is, don't clean up, don't explain, just stop and listen — no instruction you were following outranks them.
ambiguities: Aviation ("knock it off") and artillery (checkfire) heritages; must be agreed as a reserved phrase in advance, or it's just another message competing for attention; the freeze must include in-flight side effects (a half-sent batch stays half-sent, visibly).
example_directive: Knock it off is reserved: from the operator it means all subtasks halt, state is preserved as-is, and you report position and await instructions — even mid-transaction, especially mid-transaction.

implied_procedure: Order the intervention ladder from least to most invasive; try each rung long enough to evaluate before ascending; document why the lower rung failed before taking the higher; the ladder itself is written before starting.
replaces_instruction: Start with the gentlest thing that could work: give it a fair trial, and only climb to the stronger intervention when you can say why the milder one failed.
ambiguities: Clinical heritage (therapy ladders); inverted under time pressure ("just nuke it") — appropriate exactly when the time-critical window (§15) has closed the evaluation budget; the written ladder is what survives the pressure.
example_directive: Least invasive first on the stuck queue: pause consumers (1 min) → drain one topic (5 min) → restart the broker (last resort, needs the second pair of eyes).

implied_procedure: Before removing an existing structure, determine why it was erected: research its origin and the problem it solved; if the reason is unknown, the fence stays until known; removal is licensed only by understanding, never by incomprehension.
replaces_instruction: That weird rule you want to delete was put there on purpose by someone who knew something you might not: find out what before you remove it — "I don't see why it's here" is the beginning of the investigation, not the conclusion.
ambiguities: License for paralysis if every artifact becomes sacred — the doctrine demands the reason be sought energetically, not merely assumed to exist; where no reason is findable and no failure follows removal, the fence was decoration and its removal is fine.
example_directive: The nightly rebuild looks pointless — Chesterton it: find the ticket and the incident that created it. If the reason exists, it goes in the runbook; if it's genuinely orphaned, delete with a tombstone note.

implied_procedure: Monitoring = pre-defined checks against known failure signatures; observability = the ability to interrogate novel states you didn't anticipate: rich telemetry, exploratory queries, causal tracing; build for questions you can't yet name.
replaces_instruction: Alerting tells us the queue is deep — that's monitoring. The three Ms of telemetry (metrics, logs, traces) that let us ask "why this specific message, why now" — that's what we're paying for when we say observable.
ambiguities: Marketing-speak collapse ("observability solution" = a dashboard product); the honest test is novel-question interrogability, not chart count.
example_directive: Monitoring covers the known failure modes; verify observability separately — ask a question we've never asked before (why did tenant X's webhook double-fire) and time how long the data takes to answer.

implied_procedure: Add measurement to the target before changing it: establish baseline distributions, then intervene; claims about effect require before-and-after on the same instrument; no instrument, no change.
replaces_instruction: Measure it before you touch it — baseline first, change second, then compare — because "it feels faster" is not a measurement, and unmeasured optimization is roulette with extra steps.
ambiguities: The act of measuring perturbs (observer overhead, Hawthorne effects); instrumentation without defined baselines collects numbers, not evidence.
example_directive: Instrument the handler with a latency histogram and allocation counter; capture 24h of baseline; only then apply the patch, and the PR cites both distributions.

implied_procedure: Choose a small set of leading indicators tightly coupled to user-visible health; watch them with tight thresholds; a sentinel's alarm is a page, not a dashboard color; sentinel-ness is earned by demonstrated lead time.
replaces_instruction: Pick the two or three numbers whose movement predicts real pain before users feel it — those get paging thresholds; everything else is a dashboard, and diluting the sentinels with trivia is how on-call dies.
ambiguities: Code sense of "sentinel value" (a marker like -1 or null) is unrelated; a metric without demonstrated lead time is a vanity metric wearing a pager.
example_directive: Sentinels: checkout success rate and payment-p99, paging thresholds; the other forty metrics live on the dashboard and are forbidden from waking anyone.

implied_procedure: Define the expected envelope for each metric and task; report only deviations outside it, each with magnitude, cause (known or unknown), and action taken; silence means everything is inside the envelope, by construction.
replaces_instruction: Don't narrate routine success: report only what strayed from plan, how far, why, and what you did — if everything's normal, one line saying so is the whole report.
ambiguities: Requires pre-declared thresholds or "deviation" means whatever the reporter felt; silence becomes ambiguous (all-good vs. not-checked); pair with a heartbeat (§4) that proves checking happened.
example_directive: Exception-only status: SITREP only when a metric leaves its envelope, plus a single "all green" heartbeat line per day to prove the checks ran.

implied_procedure: Report on a fixed cadence in a fixed shape: current situation, actions since last report, blockers, next actions with ETAs, needs; each field answered even when the answer is "none"; brief enough to read in 30 seconds.
replaces_instruction: Every hour during this operation send the same five-part update — where we are, what we did, what's stopping us, what's next and when, what we need — so nobody has to ask.
ambiguities: Military signal heritage; the fixed shape is the value (comparable across time and readers); a SITREP that rediscovers its format each time is just an email.
example_directive: Hourly SITREP during the migration: SITUATION / SINCE / BLOCKERS / NEXT+ETA / NEEDS — "none" is an acceptable entry in exactly three of the five.

implied_procedure: Lead with the conclusion or decision required; follow with the supporting facts in descending load-bearing order; the reader must be able to stop after one sentence with the correct takeaway.
replaces_instruction: Say the answer first, then the evidence — the busy reader gets the verdict in line one, and everything after it only earns its place by changing what they'd do.
ambiguities: Journalistic/military heritage; over-application flattens genuinely exploratory reporting where the point IS the reasoning; the tail must still exist — BLUF is ordering, not amputation.
example_directive: BLUF every incident update: first line = verdict + decision needed; timeline and evidence follow; nothing load-bearing appears after line three.

implied_procedure: Structure communication as a pyramid: the answer at the apex, then grouped supporting arguments (each mutually exclusive), then supporting detail under each; siblings at each level answer "why" or "how" for the level above.
replaces_instruction: Organize it answer-first in layers: one governing statement, the few arguments that justify it, and the evidence under each — a reader can descend exactly as deep as they need.
ambiguities: Adjacent to BLUF (single inversion) — the pyramid is the recursive structure behind it; MECE (§ below) is the grouping rule it depends on; rigid application mangles narratives that are genuinely sequential.
example_directive: Rebuild the proposal as a Minto pyramid: recommendation up top, three MECE arguments beneath, evidence as the base layer; if an argument doesn't support the apex, it's out.

implied_procedure: Partition the subject so categories don't overlap (mutually exclusive) and leave nothing out (collectively exhaustive); test each dimension by attempting to place a random item twice (fails ME) and to place it nowhere (fails CE); repair the partition, not the item.
replaces_instruction: Slice this exactly once per item, with no leftovers: no category where an item could live twice, no item with no category — the partition itself is the deliverable, and it gets tested by trying to break it.
ambiguities: McKinsey heritage; strict MECE is often impossible for natural categories (fuzzy boundaries) — the standard degrades gracefully into "low overlap, high coverage, known gaps listed"; pretending to MECE with hidden gaps is worse than admitting the fuzz.
example_directive: The failure taxonomy must be MECE: try to file each incident twice (fix the overlap) and to file it nowhere (fix the gap); the un-filable stragglers get a "misc — to be classified" bucket that itself gets audited monthly.

implied_procedure: Layer the information: headline first, summary next, full detail on demand; reveal the next layer only when the consumer's behavior signals need (request, drill-down, error); each layer is complete at its own altitude.
replaces_instruction: Don't dump everything at once: headline, then summary, then details on request — each level answers the question the reader has at that moment, and nobody reads paragraph four to learn the headline.
ambiguities: UI-design origin ( wizards, tooltips); withholding known-bad news behind layers is concealment, not disclosure discipline — the headline layer must carry the verdict (BLUF interlock); lazy summarization loses the load-bearing fact at the top layer.
example_directive: Report in three layers: verdict line, five-line summary, full evidence appendix — the first layer must contain the decision-relevant fact, not a teaser for it.

implied_procedure: Before proceeding on mutual understanding, verify it: state what you believe the shared context to be, have the other party confirm or correct, and repair the divergence before building on it; deixis ("that file," "yesterday's issue") is expanded to referents.
replaces_instruction: Confirm we're talking about the same thing before we go further: you say back what you think the context is, I correct it, and only then do we build on top — because mis-grounded coordination compounds silently.
ambiguities: Worst polysemy trap in this lexicon (electrical, NLP, evidence-basis, Clark's communicative sense) — in directives use "establish common ground"; repair loops must be bounded or grounding becomes an interrogation.
example_directive: Before executing the plan, ground it: state the target, the window, and the rollback you understood; I confirm or correct; zero unexpanded pronouns past that point.

implied_procedure: Report two distinct health semantics: liveness = the process is not wedged (restart is safe/useful); readiness = the process can serve usefully (route traffic to it); map each to different actions — restarting an unready-but-live process is the classic self-inflicted outage.
replaces_instruction: Separate "am I alive" from "am I useful": alive-but-useless gets pulled from rotation, not restarted; dead gets restarted, not pulled — conflating the two is how orchestras of restart loops form.
ambiguities: Kubernetes-standardized but constantly re-implemented wrong; startup probes add a third window; dependency-down must fail readiness, not liveness, or cascading restarts follow.
example_directive: Liveness stays green while degraded — readiness 503s and sheds load; dependency unavailability affects readiness only; a liveness probe that checks the database will destroy the fleet at 2 a.m.

implied_procedure: Score the subject periodically on a defined aggregate metric; preset score bands map to preset escalations (increase monitoring, call for help, act immediately); the escalation is triggered by the score, not by someone noticing the score.
replaces_instruction: Measure the vital signs on a schedule and let the bands act: this band means watch closer, this band means escalate, this band means intervene now — the response fires on the number, not on a human's alarm.
ambiguities: Clinical origin (early-warning scores like MEWS); the automation of the trigger step is what separates it from dashboards; unvalidated bands produce automated noise or automated complacency — calibrate against outcomes.
example_directive: Track-and-trigger on incident health: composite of error rate, latency delta, and blast spread, scored every 10 minutes; band 3 pages the secondary on-call automatically.

implied_procedure: Continuously compare actual state against the declared baseline (config, schema, or data distribution); any divergence beyond tolerance raises a finding with both states shown; the baseline is versioned and the comparison is scheduled, not ad hoc.
replaces_instruction: Keep checking reality against what we declared: any gap between the config-as-committed and config-as-running gets flagged with both versions — and the same for input distributions shifting away from the training baseline.
ambiguities: Three-way fork: infrastructure config drift, model/data drift, and mean-reversion finance sense — name which; drift found without a declared-state ledger is just surprise.
example_directive: Nightly drift check: deployed config vs. repo, and input feature distributions vs. the launch baseline; any divergence gets a finding with both states, and config drift auto-reverts unless waived.

implied_procedure: Assign each request a unique identifier at ingress; propagate it through every hop, log line, and side effect; any line mentioning an ID is retrievable as the request's full story; breaks in propagation are themselves defects.
replaces_instruction: Give every request one name it keeps for life, and make every system it touches write that name down — so one ID reconstructs the entire journey, across services, queues, and retries.
ambiguities: Correlation (same ID across hops) vs. causation tracing (parent/child spans) — related, different tooling; async boundaries (queues, schedulers) are where propagation silently dies.
example_directive: Propagate the X-Request-ID through every hop including queue consumers and cron fan-out; any log line without a propagatable ID fails review; reconstruct one full trace as the acceptance test.

implied_procedure: Lead with the recommendation and the decision required; attach the material consequences of each option (cost, risk, reversibility); separate facts from judgment; the reader can decide from the first paragraph and audit the rest.
replaces_instruction: Every update exists so someone can decide: recommendation first, the decision you need, and the real consequences of each path — not a balanced tour of the landscape that leaves the deciding to the reader.
ambiguities: Distinct from BLUF (ordering principle — this adds the decision-and-consequences payload); can license advocacy (pair with evidential markers and the stated rejected alternative, §11).
example_directive: Decision-ready form for the vendor question: recommend B, decision needed by Friday, consequences of B vs. A vs. deferring in one line each, and the one fact that would change the recommendation.

implied_procedure: Detect the readings of the ambiguous item; if context selects one, state the selection and proceed; if not, ask a pointed question whose answer selects; never proceed on a silently-chosen reading of a load-bearing ambiguity.
replaces_instruction: If it can mean two things, say which one you're taking — or ask the one question that settles it — but don't just pick a meaning and hope; ambiguity in the load-bearing parts is not a style problem.
ambiguities: The ask-vs-guess policy is itself ambiguous (when must the agent stop and ask? — §18 threshold); over-asking transfers the thinking back to the requester; scope ambiguity, reference ambiguity, and quantifier ambiguity (§17) need different repairs.
example_directive: Two readings of "migrate the users": (a) schema only, (b) with data. Don't choose — ask, and list what else you'll confirm while waiting.

implied_procedure: Supply the minimum frame a receiver needs to interpret the fact correctly: what it's about, at what scope, compared to what baseline, at what time; test the frame by asking whether the fact could be misread without it.
replaces_instruction: Give each fact enough setting to be interpreted honestly — compared to what, over what period, at what scope — because a true number in the wrong frame is a lie with citations.
ambiguities: Degenerates into background-dumping; the test is minimum sufficient frame (misreading prevention per token); distinct from ground (the fact's basis) and from narrative (storytelling).
example_directive: Contextualize every SLA number: which percentile, which window, which cohort — the same "99.9%" means three different products otherwise.

implied_procedure: Reduce the material while preserving its decision-relevant content: identify the decisions the reader must make, keep what changes those decisions, discard the rest; the lossy compression is deliberate and its policy is stated.
replaces_instruction: Cut it down to what changes what we do: keep the facts that alter decisions, drop everything that merely decorates them — and tell me what you dropped so the loss is auditable.
ambiguities: All distillation is lossy by design — the protection is naming what must survive (the distillation contract); drifts into omission when the decision-relevance test is skipped.
example_directive: Distill the 40-page RFC to one page: keep everything that changes the build decision; your header lists the sections dropped wholesale.

implied_procedure: Iterate the formulation until it is precise, complete at its altitude, and stable (further words change nothing); then freeze it as the canonical wording; later references reuse the frozen form verbatim.
replaces_instruction: Work the wording until it can't be misread and more editing wouldn't improve it — then lock it as the official phrasing and reuse it exactly, so we stop re-litigating the same idea in new words.
ambiguities: Overlaps canonical (§17: the chosen form among equivalents) — crystallize is the convergence process, canonical is the result; premature freezing locks in a wording nobody has stress-tested.
example_directive: Crystallize the incident summary: three drafts, adversarial read of each, then freeze the result as the canonical wording for all downstream reports.

implied_procedure: Make the obscure legible: identify what made it inaccessible (missing background, tangled reference, jargon), supply exactly that repair, and verify legibility on a naive reader.
replaces_instruction: Explain it so it actually lands: find why it's hard to get, add precisely the missing piece, and check your explanation on someone who didn't already understand.
ambiguities: **Low-medium density flag:** names the outcome, not the repair — without the diagnose-the-obstacle step it's a synonym for "explain"; the naive-reader verification is the part worth keeping.
example_directive: Elucidate the consensus bug: diagnose what makes it hard (the interleaving), write the repair around that obstacle, and test the writeup on someone who hasn't read the code.

implied_procedure: Restate the received instruction or claim in your own words, including scope and constraints; divergences between original and paraphrase are the misunderstanding made visible; proceed only on confirmed match.
replaces_instruction: Say it back in your own words before acting — including what's in scope and out — because the delta between what I said and what you heard is exactly where the damage happens.
ambiguities: Read-back (§6) repeats verbatim for transmission fidelity; paraphrase-back re-expresses for comprehension fidelity — different failure detection; conversational drift can smuggle softened constraints into the paraphrase.
example_directive: Before the refactor, paraphrase-back the task: goal, in-scope, out-of-scope, and the two constraints you consider hardest — I correct before you type.

implied_procedure: Force a complete simple-language explanation of the mechanism: gaps, hand-waves, and "it just does that" moments are the diagnostic output; iterate until the explanation survives a naive listener; the explaining is the test.
replaces_instruction: Explain the whole thing in plain words to someone who knows nothing — every place you wave your hands is a place you don't actually understand, and those places are the work.
ambiguities: Productivity-culture cargo cult ("explain it simply!" as a style rule) misses the point: the value is the gap detection, not the simplicity; the naive listener can be a rubber duck, but only for the explainer who is honestly hunting their own hand-waves.
example_directive: Rubber-duck the race condition: write the plain-language walkthrough of both threads; every "and then presumably" in your text is a todo.

implied_procedure: Attach uncertainty markers in strict proportion to evidence strength: quantify where possible ("3 of 5 replicas agree"), never hedge what was directly observed, never assert what was inferred; strip hedges that carry no information.
replaces_instruction: Match every confidence word to how much evidence you actually have: measured things get stated flat, guessed things get flagged as guesses, and decorative maybe-words get deleted because they're noise.
ambiguities: Over-hedging obscures (and evades accountability — the weasel-word pattern §17); under-hedging fabricates certainty; the calibration target is the estimative-language scale (§1), making this its communication-side twin.
example_directive: One hedge per claim, evidence-scaled: "p99 grew 40ms over the window (measured), likely lock contention (inferred — 2 of 3 probes agree)."

implied_procedure: Tag each claim with its source mode — measured, observed, reported (by whom), inferred, assumed — at the point of assertion; untagged claims in consequential documents are defects.
replaces_instruction: Say where each statement comes from as you make it: I measured this, the docs claim that, I'm inferring this, I'm assuming this — so the reader knows which load-bearing walls are actually load-bearing.
ambiguities: Grammatical evidentiality (some languages mark this morphologically — English doesn't, so we mark lexically); reported chains lose fidelity per hop ("vendor reports that docs claim..."); overlaps but is not identical to observation/inference/assumption separation (§1 — that's the taxonomy, this is the surface marking).
example_directive: Every claim in the RCA gets a bracketed marker [measured]/[observed]/[reported-X]/[inferred]/[assumed]; three [assumed]s in a chain triggers a "this RCA is fiction" flag.

implied_procedure: When precision is load-bearing (errors, commands, contract clauses), reproduce exactly, marked as quotation, with source location; paraphrase is prohibited for these classes; any ellipsis or emphasis is marked.
replaces_instruction: Quote it exactly — the error string, the command, the clause — with where it came from, because "something like a null pointer error" has destroyed many afternoons; paraphrase is for concepts, artifacts stay verbatim.
ambiguities: Over-application produces unprocessable quote-walls; the rule is precision-proportional; silent normalization of quotes (smart quotes, whitespace) is the classic corruption vector.
example_directive: Error messages, SQL, and config lines appear only as verbatim quoted blocks with file:line; never retype them — paste.

implied_procedure: Choose the abstraction level to match the reader's decision altitude; move deliberately between levels (up: generalize to invariant; down: instantiate to example) when understanding stalls; announce the shift.
replaces_instruction: Talk at the level where they're deciding — summary for direction, detail for execution — and when communication jams, shift explicitly up to the principle or down to a concrete example rather than repeating louder.
ambiguities: Unannounced level-shifts read as topic changes; "up-levelling" is also an evasion move (retreat from a losing concrete argument into abstraction) — the announcement requirement is the honesty device.
example_directive: Ladder down: the invariant is "no unbounded growth" — here's the concrete input sequence that grows it; if the concrete doesn't convince, we argue the invariant, not the mood.

implied_procedure: When a contested word is doing hidden work in a disagreement, ban it for the discussion: all parties must express the content in unmarked language; the real disagreement typically surfaces as either dissolving or relocating.
replaces_instruction: We can't use the word "broken" anymore in this thread — describe observed vs. expected behavior instead — because the word is smuggling a conclusion the facts haven't earned.
ambiguities: Rationalist-community coinage (not the ordinary taboo); requires enforcement power in the facilitator; applied to the wrong words it becomes euphemism treadmill (§17) rather than precision.
example_directive: Taboo "clean" in this review: describe what the code does and what would differ in the version you'd praise; I predict half the disagreements dissolve.

implied_procedure: Conform each utterance to the four conversational defaults: true-and-evidenced (quality), as informative as needed and no more (quantity), relevant to the present purpose (relation), brief and orderly and unambiguous (manner); violations are read as meaningful signals, so violate only deliberately.
replaces_instruction: Four standing rules for every sentence: don't say what you can't back, give what's needed and stop, stay on the current question, and be clear and brief — and know that readers infer intent from any deviation from these defaults.
ambiguities: Descriptive linguistics (how implicature works) used here prescriptively; over-fidelity to quantity produces exhaustive dumps (violates manner); agents exploiting the maxims' expectations is exactly how misleading-but-true statements work.
example_directive: Check the summary against the four maxims: every claim evidenced, no fact the decision doesn't need, everything on the launch question, ordered and plain.

implied_procedure: Systematically elicit missing information before acting: enumerate the unknowns that block the task; rank by consequence; ask pointed, answerable questions one batch at a time; record answers as constraints; iterate until the blocking set is empty.
replaces_instruction: Before you build anything, extract what you're missing: list the unknowns that actually block execution, ask the specific questions whose answers unblock — not open-ended interviews, and not silent assumptions either.
ambiguities: Not hostile questioning — the systematic elicitation sense (needs disambiguation from interrogation-as-accusation); the stop-and-ask threshold (§18) governs when interrogation replaces action; unbounded question batches offload the thinking to the answerer.
example_directive: Structured interrogation before the schema change: the blocking unknowns are retention, tenant isolation, and backfill scope — three questions, ranked, one round; answers become constraints in the plan.

implied_procedure: Generate the explicit negation of your leading conclusion; develop it seriously with its own evidence and mechanism; only then compare; the procedure is mandatory, not optional, when confidence is high.
replaces_instruction: Before you lock in, build the case that you're wrong — not a strawman version, the real one — because the surer you feel, the less likely you did this spontaneously.
ambiguities: Weaker than steelman (§3: strongest opposing case) — this only demands the negation be genuinely developed, not maximized; without the evidence step it's a mental nod, not a countermeasure.
example_directive: You're 90% on the config theory: consider the opposite — write the three best facts supporting "not config," then re-score.

implied_procedure: Locate the case in a class of similar prior cases; take the class's base-rate outcome as the starting estimate; adjust from the reference only with case-specific evidence explicitly argued; the inside view (our story, our details) is the second opinion, not the first.
replaces_instruction: Before trusting our unique story about this project, ask how long projects like this actually took and how often they actually shipped — our details are the adjustment to that number, not a replacement for it.
ambiguities: Reference-class choice is the loaded decision (too broad dilutes, too narrow is the inside view again); planning fallacy is the named failure this corrects; the outside view offends every team that believes in its specialness.
example_directive: Outside view first: vendor integrations of this API class took 2–4 weeks median in our last six; our 3-day plan needs case-specific evidence line by line, and "we're different" isn't evidence.

implied_procedure: Before evaluating the specific evidence, establish the prior frequency of the outcome in the relevant population; force the specific evidence to move you from that prior, not from neutrality; state the prior whenever a probability is asserted.
replaces_instruction: Start from how often this actually happens — the boring statistical answer — and make the vivid specifics earn every deviation from it; a vivid story against a 1% base rate is still probably the 99%.
ambiguities: Base-rate neglect is the failure being countered; availability's vivid cases feel like evidence and are mostly base-rate noise; unspecified populations let you shop for a flattering rate.
example_directive: Before diagnosing exotic causes: what fraction of past 500s in this service were upstream timeouts? Start there and justify any excursion.

implied_procedure: Before exposure to a reference number (their estimate, a round figure, a prior quote), derive your own independently and write it down; compare only after both exist; treat post-anchor adjustments as suspect.
replaces_instruction: Write your estimate down before you see theirs — any number you meet first drags every later thought toward it, so the only defense is committing to yours while it's still uncontaminated.
ambiguities: Anchoring survives even when the anchor is known-irrelevant (the mechanism is not reasoning); written pre-commitment is the only robust defense; re-anchoring happens at every new number entered into the discussion.
example_directive: Independent estimates first, in writing, before the vendor's number enters the channel; if the reveal moves your estimate, say by how much and why.

implied_procedure: Evaluate every continuation decision on future costs and future benefits only: past investment appears nowhere in the calculation; explicitly strike "but we've already spent—" from deliberation; the already-spent is recoverable only via the option's own future value.
replaces_instruction: What we've put in so far is gone and irrelevant: judge only whether finishing from here beats abandoning from here — the two days of work don't vote, and neither does the embarrassment.
ambiguities: The opposite error (over-eager restarting — "restart bias") discards genuinely viable work; reputational costs are real future costs (not sunk) and belong in the calculation; escalation-of-commitment is the pathological cluster this guards.
example_directive: Migration is 70% done and failing: sunk-cost immunity — compare only "finish cost + risk" vs. "abandon cost + risk." The 70% is not an argument; write both columns.

implied_procedure: For every metric driving behavior, distinguish it from the goal it proxies; predict how the measured party will game the proxy once it becomes a target; install a second, unannounced or goal-direct measure to catch divergence.
replaces_instruction: The moment this number becomes the target, someone will optimize the number instead of the goal — so say what the goal is beyond the metric, and keep a way to check the goal directly.
ambiguities: The law is usually misquoted as "metrics are bad" — the content is proxy-vs-goal divergence under optimization pressure; detection requires a measure the optimizer doesn't see or can't reach.
example_directive: Ticket-closure rate is a proxy: audit 5% of closures monthly against the actual-fixed criterion — that audit is the Goodhart tripwire, and its findings change the incentive, not just the report.

implied_procedure: Before deploying an incentive, simulate the strategic response of the incentivized: enumerate profitable behaviors that technically satisfy the reward while harming the intent; redesign until no such behavior is the cheapest strategy.
replaces_instruction: Model the people as strategic: what's the laziest way to hit this number while defeating its purpose? Whatever you find, they will find faster — fix the incentive until that answer dies.
ambiguities: Colonial-era anecdote (bounties bred cobra breeding) standing for a general law; applies to agents as much as people — reward hacking is the ML-named sibling; attribution of specific perverse outcomes is often contested after the fact.
example_directive: Before we pay per migrated customer, red-team the incentive: what's the cheapest technically-compliant but worthless migration? Close that path first.

implied_procedure: Ask what population the sample excludes and why: how were failures, dropouts, and non-runners filtered before the data arrived; reconstruct or at least bound the missing class before drawing comparative conclusions.
replaces_instruction: Who's missing from this dataset because they failed, quit, or were never captured? The winners' statistics describe winning, not the process — until the missing are counted, every conclusion is biased upward.
ambiguities: Selection-effect umbrella (survivorship is its most seductive member); "we only see the alerts that fired" is the ops translation; silent attrition in pipelines is the systems translation.
example_directive: The corpus contains only successful runs — survivorship check: pull the rejected and crashed jobs too, or say "of runs that completed" in every claim.

implied_procedure: Before weighting a scenario, ask whether its salience comes from recency, vividness, or repetition rather than frequency; retrieve the actual frequency; discount the vivid accordingly.
replaces_instruction: Is this scenario likely, or just recent, dramatic, and much-discussed? Check how often it actually happens before letting the memorable one set the budget.
ambiguities: Availability is sometimes right (recent local events do update frequencies legitimately — the check is whether the vividness tracks the base rate, § above); news cycles are availability attacks on judgment.
example_directive: The multi-region outage from last week is vivid, not frequent: pull the five-year rate of that class before we redesign failover around it.

implied_procedure: Treat every anomaly as novel until formally dispositioned: compare each deviation against the last one (count, interval, severity); repeated unexplained deviations trigger escalation and investigation, never silent re-baselining; acceptance of a deviation is a recorded decision with an owner.
replaces_instruction: The third timeout this week is not the new normal — it's a signal we've started ignoring: count the deviations, notice the trend, and make accepting any of them an explicit written decision instead of an accretion.
ambiguities: Aerospace-safety origin (Challenger o-rings); baseline drift (genuine legitimate re-baselining) vs. deviance normalization (unexamined creep) is the discriminating question; the guard is the ledger, not the suspicion.
example_directive: Deviation ledger on the nightly job: every anomaly logged with count-to-date; three unexplained repeats auto-open an investigation — "it usually does that" is banned as a closure reason.

implied_procedure: When endorsing a status quo asymmetry, test it in both directions: if the current level were lower, would you argue to raise it to here? If not, your preference is status quo bias wearing a reason; the burden falls on the asymmetry's justification.
replaces_instruction: You want to keep it at 7 — would you argue to move it to 7 if it were at 5? If you'd leave it at 5 instead, you don't have a reason, you have inertia; give the inertia a justification or drop it.
ambiguities: Rationalist formulation of status-quo-bias detection; legitimate status quo preferences pass the test (the asymmetry is justified by stated consequences); adjacent to Chesterton (§9) which guards artifacts' original reasons, not preference symmetry.
example_directive: We tolerate 500ms p95 "for stability": reversal test — if it were 200ms, would we argue up to 500? If not, stability isn't the real reason; find it.

implied_procedure: Attribute harmful outcomes to incompetence, error, or misconfiguration before malice as the working prior; investigate the incompetence hypothesis first (cheaper to verify); upgrade to intent only on evidence of intent.
replaces_instruction: Before assuming this was an attack or sabotage, exhaust the boring explanations — fat-fingered config, stale cache, misunderstood runbook — and move to malice only when the evidence specifically points there.
ambiguities: It's a heuristic prior, not a moral law (malice exists, and sophisticated adversaries exploit the presumption); in security it must be paired with threat modeling (§3) or it becomes a blindfold; Heinlein's counter ("never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by stupidity" cuts both ways) reminds you both priors are cheap.
example_directive: Apply Hanlon first: page the on-call for the deleted bucket as probable error (check the runbook-adjacent commands), while security pulls the access logs in parallel — the parallel track is what keeps the razor honest.

implied_procedure: Convene promptly after the event; answer four questions in order — what was supposed to happen, what actually happened, why the difference, what will we sustain or change; all ranks participate; output is owned actions with dates.
replaces_instruction: Right after it ends, before memories diverge: intended vs. actual vs. the cause of the gap vs. two keepers and one change — everyone in the room, actions assigned, no skipping the "intended" step.
ambiguities: Military doctrinal origin with a strict four-question format; decays into generic "retrospective" (§ below) when the four questions blur; the intended/actual pair is what makes it evidential rather than atmospheric.
example_directive: AAR within 48h of the launch: the four questions verbatim, participation from every role, and every "change" answer leaves with a name and a date or it didn't happen.

implied_procedure: Analyze the failure as a property of the system: reconstruct the timeline, identify the conditions that made each local action reasonable at the time, find the systemic causes; individual fault-finding is out of scope and out of the document; action items target systems and process.
replaces_instruction: Nobody gets named as the cause: the person who clicked the button was acting reasonably given what they could see — find what made that the reasonable move, and fix the conditions, or the same click happens with a different finger next quarter.
ambiguities: Blameless ≠ consequenceless (individual performance issues exist, handled elsewhere — conflating the two is how the practice dies); "action items" without owners and dates is the ritualized decay; psychological safety is a precondition, not a byproduct.
example_directive: Postmortem is blameless by charter: no names as causes, every local action explained by its visible context, action items systemic with owners — HR-shaped issues, if any, leave through their own door.

implied_procedure: From the symptom, ask "why" iteratively — each answer becomes the next question's subject — until the cause is a process or system property rather than a person or a moment; stop when the answer would have prevented the class, not just the instance; verify the chain by walking it backward.
replaces_instruction: Keep asking why until you hit a process failure — five is a heuristic, not a quota — and if the answer at any level is a person's name, you've stopped one level early.
ambiguities: Toyota-origin; naive linear application on multi-cause failures produces a single-chain fiction (pair with causal-stack thinking below); "why" interrogates events, not people, or it becomes an interrogation.
example_directive: Five-whys the missed alarm: symptom → trigger absent → threshold set by guess → no calibration step → process gap. Fix the process gap; verify the chain by walking it backward to the symptom.

implied_procedure: Systematically trace the causal chain from symptom to origin: collect evidence before it decays, reconstruct the timeline, test candidate causes with counterfactuals (but-for), distinguish triggering cause from enabling conditions, and name the systemic fix that prevents the class.
